name: Kinhouse Open Door: 2027 Exhibition & Residency Open Call
eligibility_details:
**Call Ends:** October 11th, 2026, 11:59pm ET
**Artist’s Notified by:** October 21st, 2026

**Exhibition and residency dates will be determined at the time of proposal selection.** Residencies are for 6 nights, check in Monday and check out Sunday. The exhibition reception will be on the Friday evening of the residency week (coordinating dates below).

**Artists will choose from 4 options:**
March 1st - 7th, 2026 (exhibition opening March 5th)
May 31st - June 6th, 2026 (exhibition opening June 4th)
June 28th - July 4th, 2026 (exhibition opening July 2nd)
August 2nd - 8th, 2026 (exhibition opening August 6th)

The exhibition will be up in our gallery space for the duration of the month following the “First Friday” reception opening.

**Installation and deinstallation support** will be provided, however each proposal may have different needs. For proposals that require detailed artist oversight, the artist(s) should be available for installation and/or deinstallation in person at our exhibition space in Fort Wayne, IN. If the artist(s) cannot be present for deinstallation, Kinhouse staff will deinstall and arrange pick up. If the work needs to be shipped back to the artist(s), artists must provide shipping materials and pay for return shipping.

**To get a better idea of our space:** please view our instagram: @kinhouseart or check our FLOOR PLAN here.

**Origin of Work**

- All artwork must be original in design and personal execution.
- Artworks must be the artist’s original work. No commercially made prints, giclees, or reproductions of an original work of art will be considered for exhibition.

**Condition of Artwork at Dropoff, if Accepted**

- Artwork must have been created by the applicant within the past two years. Artwork must not have been previously displayed at the Delaplaine. Artwork must remain on view for the duration of the exhibit. Artists are solely responsible for artwork preparation, delivery, and pick up.
- Accepted two-dimensional, wall-hanging work does not need to be framed but does need to be wired to a professional standard, delivered ready to hang. NO SAWTOOTH HANGERS; they do not work with the Delaplaine’s professional hanging system. Wire should be affixed to the frame using D-ring or strap hangers in one smooth line. Please make sure that the picture hanging wire used is a suitable strength for the weight of your work. Framed work should be secured using offset clips and screws (works on canvas) or using points (flat works with backing board). ABSOLUTELY NO TAPE, DUCT TAPE, MASKING TAPE, OR OTHER UNSTABLE METHODS FOR SECURING WORK TO ITS FRAME.
- Accepted work may be refused because of framing or condition.
- Artists accepted into the exhibition will be provided with a drop-off form and label for the back in the top right-hand corner with the following information:
- Artist name
- Title
- Medium
- Sale price or not for sale (NFS) indication with insurance value
- Preferred phone number
- Email address

eligibility_details:
**ELIGIBILITY**

This opportunity is open to all Chicago based professional artists, artists teams, and arts organizations.

Applicants may indicate that they would like to be considered for both sites. However, if selected, an artist or artist team will be chosen as a finalist for only one site. Each site commission will be awarded to a different artist or artist team.

**SELECTION PROCESS**

Following the RFQ application deadline, DCASE will convene a selection panel of community representatives, arts professionals, and 35th Ward staff to review the applications.

The committee will select 3 finalists per site, who will be commissioned to develop public art proposals. Finalists will present their design proposals to the selection committee, and a final artist or artist team will be selected for each site.

**SELECTION CRITERIA**

Applications will be reviewed by a selection panel composed of community representatives, arts professionals, and 35th Ward staff. The panel will evaluate submissions using a rubric that considers the following general criteria:

**Creative Practice**
The artistic quality, originality, and professional experience demonstrated through the applicant’s portfolio of past work, particularly large-scale exterior mural projects.

**Community Relevance**
The artist’s ability to create work that is responsive to the surrounding community and demonstrates an understanding of place and public engagement.

**Administrative and Project Management Capacity**
The artist’s ability to successfully plan and execute a mural project, including collaboration with project partners, communication with stakeholders, and the management of timelines and project requirements.

name: Public Art Archive - Call for Artwork Submissions
eligibility_details: The Public Art Archive accepts submissions of completed public art projects from artists and commissioning agencies. PAA defines public art as any work of art that is (or was at one time, if a temporary work) situated in a location that is accessible or viewable by the general public at no cost. Works of art that were commissioned and/or gifted by corporations, museums, educational institutions, private parties, and other entities may also be eligible. New media, performative, rotating, and portable works may be eligible if they meet the commonly known definition of public art or civic art and are/were accessible for public viewing free of charge. Gallery art and art exhibited inside galleries and museums is typically not eligible. If you have questions about your artwork’s eligibility, please contact the Public Art Archive team at PAArchive@westaf.org
